problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for $f(x)={log}_{2}⁡x$ on the interval $[4,16].$
worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[4,16]$ and differentiable on $(4,16),$ hence, we can apply the Mean Value Theorem. 

So, the mean value theorem states that there exists a $c\in (4,16)$ such that

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

Plugging in $a=4$ and $b=16$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(16)-f(4)}{16-4} \\  & =\frac{{log}_{2}⁡(16)-{log}_{2}⁡(4)}{12} \\  & =\frac{4-2}{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{2}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{1}{c\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{c\operatorname{ln}⁡2} & =\frac{1}{6} \\ c & =\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$
